page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v5 is a low-memory, compute-oriented virtual machine instance belonging to the DLSv5 family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8370C processor cores operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, with hyper-threading enabled to provide two threads per core. System memory is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations position the D32ls_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. The Intel Xeon 8370C processor achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1682.0 and a multi-core score of 14191.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 36834.55. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only performance of 1668.94 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 150.05 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small language models at 293.87 tokens/sec, though performance drops to a weak 6.66 tokens/sec for prompt processing on large models due to the lack of hardware acceleration and lower memory density.

The D32ls_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy applications that do not require large memory footprints or local disk storage. By reducing the RAM-to-vCPU ratio to 1:2, it minimizes memory overhead costs while retaining high-density CPU processing power. This configuration is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, text processing, and moderate database operations. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs makes it less suitable for high-throughput local storage indexing or large-scale deep learning training.
